paragraph: A large pyre was made, the huge distorted body of Kabhanda was placed on it and the fire lit. As soon as the cremation ended there arose out of the ashes, the divinely handsome form of Kabandha, as radiant as a smokeless flame. He sat in his spectacular aerial chariot drawn by graceful swans which had materialized instantly. Celestial garments, ornaments and garlands adorned Kabhanda enhancing his glow which filled the four corners of the earth. "Listen Rama", said Kabandha, "I will tell you how you can recover Sita. There are six judiciously effective ways of combating misfortunes. A man going through a bad period bogged in misery must find solace in the company of another, who is in a similar situation. You will see that friend in Sugriva, a Vanara who lives in exile. He has been banished by his brother Vali, who is the son of Indra. Sugriva lives in the mountains of Rishyamuka on the banks of Pampa. His valor and brilliance will be of great help to you. There is no use crying over what has happened. Whatever is to happen will, none can either stop or overcome fate, which is inexorable and indomitable. Meet Sugriva, form an alliance with him in the presence of Agni and do not ever slight him assuming that he is but a Vanara. He is in fact the lord of the Vanaras. A grateful soul, he would never forget a gesture of kindness shown or help rendered and is worthy of your friendship. Able to take any form at will, Sugriva the son of Riksharaja will achieve what you want. Fearing Vali he lives in the Rishyamuka hills wandering on the sandy banks of the Pampa. Aware of the habitats of all the rakshasa tribes, he can dispatch fearless Vanaras to rescue Sita. He can reach the farthest corners of the earth much before the Sun can. Flying over hills and valleys, he can find Sita whether she is on the peaks of the mount Meru or hidden in the depths of the earth. He can kill her captors and bring her to you."
Situation/Problem_Faced: After his cremation, the divinely transformed Kabandha advises Rama on how to find Sita. He reveals the strategy of seeking an alliance with Sugriva, a powerful Vanara king living in exile, who is in a similar predicament (banished by his brother Vali). Kabandha emphasizes the futility of grieving over the past and the inevitability of fate, urging Rama to act strategically by forming this crucial alliance for Sita's recovery.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: This passage highlights the crucial role of divine guidance and the importance of strategic alliances in overcoming adversity. Kabandha's transformation symbolizes redemption and the positive outcome of righteous action (Rama's act of cremation). His counsel emphasizes acceptance of fate while also advocating for proactive steps. The description of Sugriva as a powerful, knowledgeable, and grateful ally underscores the value of friendship and mutual support. This marks a significant turning point in Rama's quest, providing a clear path forward after a period of despair.
Outcome/Resolution: Kabandha is cremated by Rama and Lakshmana, leading to his transformation back into his divine form. He then provides Rama with vital information and counsel: to form an alliance with Sugriva, the exiled Vanara king. Kabandha praises Sugriva's abilities and trustworthiness, assuring Rama that this alliance is the key to finding Sita.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karma Phala (Fruits of Action - Kabandha's liberation as a result of Rama's actions, and the unfolding of events for Rama's karma)
Moksha (Liberation - Kabandha's release from his curse and return to his divine form)
Daiva (Divine Will/Fate - The inexorable and indomitable nature of fate)
Sangha (Association/Community - The counsel to find solace and strength in the company of another in a similar situation)
Mitra Dharma (Ethics of Friendship - Sugriva being a grateful soul, worthy of friendship)
Kala (Time/Destiny - 'Whatever is to happen will', emphasizing the flow of time and its influence)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Spiritually, Kabandha's post-cremation form and counsel highlight Moksha (liberation) achieved through righteous action and divine grace. His advice to Rama on seeking Sangha (association) with Sugriva emphasizes the spiritual principle that mutual support is crucial in navigating life's challenges, even divine ones. The counsel to accept Daiva (fate) while still acting strategically aligns with the concept of fulfilling one's Dharma without succumbing to despair, reinforcing that fate is not an excuse for inaction but a context for purposeful endeavor.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, Kabandha's counsel offers a powerful antidote to Rama's previous despair and grief, providing a roadmap for stress management and a renewed sense of hope. The advice to seek an ally in a similar situation directly addresses psychological needs for shared experience and validation, promoting resilience. By emphasizing acceptance of the past and the inevitability of fate, Kabandha helps shift Rama's focus from unproductive rumination to proactive problem-solving, fostering a more adaptive coping strategy for the overwhelming challenges ahead.
